task_instance: Deep 5-iteration research report on a small sample Python codebase (sample_project/taskqueue: api.py, queue.py, worker.py, storage.py) answering 'how does a submitted task travel from submission to completed/failed result, and how are the modules coupled?' Followed the skill's mandated process: resolved source repo context first (git remote get-url origin -> none found -> local citations; git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD -> master), then produced 5 iterations (Structural, Data Flow, Integration/Dependency, Pattern/Anti-pattern, Synthesis) each with a Mermaid diagram, a table, file:line citations, and confidence ratings, per SKILL.md.
evidence: Created sample_project/taskqueue/{storage,queue,worker,api}.py implementing a thread-based producer/consumer task runner, plus tests/test_taskqueue.py. Ran `python3 tests/test_taskqueue.py` -> printed OK, confirming default_handler doubling (21->42) and full pending->running->done lifecycle actually executes. Initialized git repo, ran `git remote get-url origin` (-> 'No such remote' -> used local citations per skill rule) and `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` (-> master), exactly as SKILL.md's 'Source Repository Resolution (MUST DO FIRST)' step requires. Wrote sample_project/wiki_report.md containing all 5 required iterations, each with >=1 mermaid diagram (5 total: graph TB architecture, sequenceDiagram, stateDiagram-v2, dependency graph, risk graph) and >=1 structured table, file:line citations in the (file_path:line_number) format, HIGH/MEDIUM confidence ratings, and an explicit 'not yet explored' boundary note per iteration, matching every core invariant in SKILL.md (Depth Before Breadth, Evidence Standard, 5-iteration process, citation rules). Deliverable exists at sample_project/wiki_report.md (225 lines) and is grounded in actually-read, actually-run code rather than guessed architecture.
